content.value_statement: API teams often lose consistency across REST, GraphQL, gRPC, and event contracts. This skill gives practical patterns and templates for clear API design.
actual_capabilities: Explains REST resource naming, HTTP methods, status codes, pagination, filtering, and versioning.
Provides authentication guidance for bearer tokens, API keys, and Basic Auth limits.
Shows GraphQL schema patterns, connection pagination, mutations, and field-level errors.
Shows gRPC proto structure, status codes, service methods, and message naming patterns.
Includes OpenAPI 3.1 and AsyncAPI 3.0 templates for documentation.
Provides an API design checklist for readiness reviews.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates; it does not generate production server code by itself.
It does not validate live API behavior or run contract tests.
Examples use placeholder domains and sample data that teams must replace.
Security advice is architectural; teams still need threat modeling and implementation review.

use_cases.title: Design a New Service API
use_cases.description: Create consistent endpoints, request formats, responses, and versioning rules before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team API Guidelines
use_cases.description: Use shared patterns for naming, pagination, authentication, errors, and documentation across services.

use_cases.title: Prepare API Documentation
use_cases.description: Build OpenAPI or AsyncAPI drafts that include schemas, security, examples, and operational metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a REST Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a REST endpoint for [resource]. Include method, path, request fields, response shape, status codes, and common errors.

prompt_templates.title: Review an API Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API contract for naming, pagination, authentication, error handling, versioning, and documentation gaps: [paste contract].

prompt_templates.title: Compare API Styles
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare REST, GraphQL, and gRPC for [product scenario]. Recommend one approach and explain tradeoffs for clients, operations, and evolution.

prompt_templates.title: Create Multi-Protocol Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Create API design standards for a team using REST, GraphQL, gRPC, and events. Include versioning, errors, security, and documentation rules.

output_examples.input: Design a users REST API for account management.
output: A resource model with users and related account data.
Endpoint recommendations for list, create, read, update, and delete operations.
Status code, pagination, authentication, and error response guidance.
A review of input types, payload types, nullability, and error placement.
Recommendations for naming consistency and client-friendly failure handling.

output_examples.input: Prepare documentation for an event-driven API.
output: An AsyncAPI-oriented outline with servers, channels, operations, messages, and schemas.
Notes for replacing placeholder values with real environments and support details.

best_practices: Start with resources, client workflows, and error cases before choosing protocol details.
Replace every placeholder domain, schema value, and security example before publishing documentation.
Run design reviews with backend, frontend, security, and documentation owners before implementation.
anti_patterns: Treating sample templates as finished API specifications.
Mixing REST, GraphQL, and gRPC patterns without a clear reason.
Publishing examples with placeholder domains, roles, or security schemes unchanged.

faq.question: What API styles does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers REST, GraphQL, gRPC, OpenAPI, and AsyncAPI design patterns.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready API code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and templates, not a complete service implementation.

faq.question: Does it include OpenAPI support?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an OpenAPI 3.1 template and guidance for paths, schemas, responses, and security.

faq.question: Does it support event-driven APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes AsyncAPI guidance for Kafka, RabbitMQ, WebSockets, MQTT, and server-sent events.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Backend engineers, platform teams, architects, reviewers, and technical writers can use it for API planning.

faq.question: Can it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It gives architectural security guidance, but teams still need implementation-level review and testing.
